newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE STOCKS CLOSE LOWER, SEEN SOFT.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE STOCKS CLOSE LOWER, SEEN SOFT.

text.p: Argentine stocks skidded lower at the close Tuesday on the back of a selling bout which erased early gains on the U.S. markets, dealers said.
"The bolsa was unable to resist the fall in U.S. Treasuries again today, because it had already bucked the (downward) trend Monday and Friday," said Rodrigo Diz at traders Velox Inversiones.
Blue chips slipped off an early high of 856 on the weighted MerVal index to close at 841.05 with a loss of 1.4 percent.
"Things suddenly changed. I guess we thought the long bond yield had stabilized, but then it crept back up towards 6.7 percent," another dealer said.
The long bond yield closed at 6.67 percent against 6.61 percent at the opening, while the Dow suffered a loss of more than 100 points.

"This shows lingering interest rate worries," the dealer said. "However, this volatility is normal, because the Federal Reserve meets in a week's time to discuss rates and tomorrow's retail sales data could show whether the U.S. economy is growing too fast to keep inflation flat in the third quarter."
The broad market index managed to stay in positive territory, closing up 0.1 percent, but losing issues beat winners 31 to 17 and 14 stocks closed unchanged.
Floor volume recovered to 31.4 million pesos from a token 17.5 million traded Monday, while over-the-counter turnover slowed to 103.1 million pesos from 111.5 million Monday.

Carmakers Sevel and Ciadea led main-tier losses, reeling 10 percent and 9.9 percent, respectively. Traders blamed the fall on disappointing first-half results and some recurring trade tension with Brazil, Argentina's main partner in the customs union Mercosur.
Pulp and paper maker Celulosa, a highly volatile stock, also tumbled 9.4 percent.
The only MerVal gainers were steelmaker Siderar, which climbed 1.9 percent, Telefonica and Telecom, up 1.5 percent and 1.2 percent, respectively, and oil giant YPF, up 0.3 percent.
